steps.body: A circle has no ends, so the counter must invent one: remember the starting bead, and stop just before reaching it again.
steps.narration: A circle has no ends, so the counter must invent one: remember the starting bead, and stop just before reaching it again.

widget.prompt: Count 7 beads from a circle — one counter per bead, stopping at the start.

commonCounts.feedback: The count passed its starting bead and counted it twice; a circle needs a remembered start.
One bead was missed — going once around must touch every bead exactly once.

widget.missFeedback: Pick a starting bead, count around, and stop just before reaching it again.
widget.successFeedback: Seven counters, and the count stopped exactly where it began.

predict.prompt: Counting a circle of beads without marking the start, what is the risk?
predict.reveal: With no ends to stop you, the count can lap the circle and recount the first beads.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch count circle.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch count circle.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

widget.prompt: Counting beads in a circle, what must you remember?

options.label: Remember where you started
options.feedback: Correct — a circle has no natural end, so the starting bead marks where the count must stop.

options.label: To count the biggest bead first
options.feedback: Size plays no part in counting; each bead gets one number wherever you begin.

options.label: To count twice around to be sure
options.feedback: Twice around counts every bead twice, doubling the answer.

options.label: To skip the bead you started on
options.feedback: The starting bead is counted once — it is RE-counting it that must be avoided.

options.feedback: Correct — the last number said, 5, tells how many blocks there are in all.
The count stops at 5; saying one more number would count a block that is not there.
That stops one number early — every block gets exactly one number, ending at 5.
That runs two past the count; the last number spoken is the answer, and it was 5.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 10? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 10 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 11.
12 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 10 lands on 11.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 10 and count on 1: you land on 11.
widget.successFeedback: 11 — one hop forward, because each number is exactly one more than the last.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 11.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 10 means one hop, stopping on 11.
